items.a: Around **8 a.m.**, Ryan Dahl announced **Seld** (he said **Seld these nuts**). Apache 2, self-hosted durable objects and workers, V8, S3, SQLite, R2-style storage, experimental containers. A cost comparison where durable objects get **cheaper than Cloudflare**.
Around **8 a.m.**, about **two months** later, the Deno team joins **Cloudflare** because of Seld. **Kenton Varda** will champion it.

items.q: What did the 2018 regrets say, and what happened?
items.a: He would not be **Node-compatible**, or he would just rebuild Node. He faulted **package.json**, npm, and a missing sandbox. The host says that last year about **50% of Deno commits**, and about half the lines, were **Node compatibility**.

One more year of **monthly bug and security releases**, then development stops. The runtime stays open source. **Deno Deploy** runs **six more months**, then shuts down, with migration help for paying customers onto **Cloudflare Workers**.

items.q: What is a durable object, in the sense he uses?
items.a: An **individually addressable single-threaded server** with its own **SQLite**. It sleeps when idle. That is the 2021 Cloudflare idea he says Seld was selling.
